ROOT_CAUSE.classification: A (implementation defect) for the first two; B (invalid cross-platform test expectation) for DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS; the termination failure is their truthful nested consequence
ROOT_CAUSE.A: The R5 rewrite of the inner PowerShell script regressed portability relative to R4 (green on the same runner): it set PSModulePath to empty before its only module-qualified cmdlet (ConvertFrom-Json), and PowerShell 7 on Linux then failed the plan read (exit 1 before the node pin, for both failing tests); and it built the launcher path from a backslash-joined literal, which cannot exist on Linux (R4 used Join-Path). Locally Windows PowerShell 5.1 still resolved the module and accepted backslashes, which masked both. The rejection paths (NODE_*, COR_PROFILER, CORECLR_PROFILER) passed on Linux because they refuse before the plan read.
ROOT_CAUSE.B: DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS is a CoreCLR host feature. Measured locally: the governed inner shell, Windows PowerShell 5.1, runs on .NET Framework 4.8.9345.0, which does not implement startup hooks, so the script runs and refuses the variable. On Linux CI the shell is PowerShell 7 (CoreCLR); its host resolved the (absent) hook before any script line and the process ended by signal. The expectation 'the inner script refuses it on every runtime' is false for CoreCLR; it is also exactly why the governed Windows entry clears the variable in the outer cmd before PowerShell starts.
